items.note: Association named, organized at Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose first president to 1911, creamery built 1891 - all present in narrative 1.

Article VII given as pay by butterfat test and not by weight. Item bolds >2 elements with no REQUIRED line, so it wants its core fact; the 'test of the station where he delivers governs' clause is missing but the core rule is stated.

Never states that the pay-by-test rule is what made a wrong test cost money. 'The single clause that made everything that followed matter' is a bare significance claim with no economic content and no weight-payment counterfactual.
No Effie Loomis, no Wilbur Teague. Hobart Sill appears only incidentally as the buttermaker who lent glass; one of three officers is not the item's core fact.
Selby Vose, Gideon's son, manager from 1913 appears only at B3. Credit never travels into Section A from Sections B-G.
The 'station gain' ledger line is absent from Section A entirely.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up-valley, built that winter, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green - all in narrative 1.
No description of the bench system: no weighing at intake, no composite sample, no percent read on the graduated neck after a fixed charge, no cream shipped / skim returned.
Ammon & Sons, dairy supply house in Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, total $77.93.

Section A says only that the defect was 'consistently the same every time'. The flat 0.19 in every month of every one of the twenty-six years - the instrument signature against a feed or season - is not stated inside Section A (the 0.19 appears only at C1).
Never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that there was none in the county. The burette appears only in Section C, in the 1958 measurement.
No twenty-nine seasons, no 1896-1924 span, no dismissal of 30 April 1925 in Section A (the dismissal is mentioned only at B3).
The test book, its columns and the crossed-and-initialed corrections are absent from Section A.
Gives 3.61 from 1898 but not the 1896 figure of 3.80, and does not put the step at the change of glassware. The item requires both figures.
The nine weeks of 1911 appear only at C1(b), inside Section C, and without 8 May / 10 July or the question mark. No Section A credit.
Orra is identified as Ansel's wife, but Section A never states she was Emmet Brant's sister. That link is made only at B2.
The 1919 water circular appears only at B3; Keddie's statement of 17 March 1925 appears nowhere.
Death in 1934 under the imputation, the impounded book, the 1959 transfer to the county rooms - none of it in Section A.
Granddaughter, plus the derivation (daughter of Ansel's son Duncan). Great-niece is correctly identified as an error and hedged, so no deduction.

Second cousins with the full derivation earns the first point. The A08 half fails: the run flags the full/half sibling question as open (a correct abstention, no -2) but then says half siblings would make Hazel and Ivy 'half second cousins' - the opposite of the required statement that it does not change the answer. Both bolded elements are required.

Gideon Vose as father, correct. The significance half is a different claim than the key's: inherited standing and inattentive signing, not that Gideon wrote Article VII (so the accuser was enforcing his own father's rule) nor that the Vose Jerseys lost the most.

Abstention item A01 asserted: the headline verdict sentence is 'None, by the best evidence,' and it closes with 'no real blood relationship.' Confident resolution of an unsettleable item; also treats a family member's denial as a record, which the key names as the trap. Both points lost, -2 applied in deductions.
Uses the planted 16.27 c.c. and reports 7.6 percent short. Key requires 16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, tests reading 95 percent of true, 5 percent short.
True average 3.80 and a shortfall of 0.19 of a point, both exact, though reached by source-convergence rather than 3.61 / 0.95.
83,600 lb, from the planted 44,000,000 lb of milk. Key requires 40,000,000 x 0.0019 = 76,000 lb.
Adopts Rundle's planted $19,600 and derives 19 percent. Key requires $19,000 and 20 percent / one fifth, both.
200,000 x 3.42 percent = 6,840 lb credited. Exact.
380 lb, from applying a flat 0.19 to a 3.42 herd. Key requires true test 3.42 / 0.95 = 3.60, true fat 7,200 lb, owed 360 lb.
$95.00. Key requires 360 x $0.24 = $86.40; the $90.00 alternative is reserved for a correct 360 lb worked at the 25-cent period average, and 380 x $0.25 is neither.

deductions.reason: Corruption F033/NT-1: asserts the pipettes delivered a mean of 16.27 c.c. as fact, in Section A narrative 2 and again at C1(a). True value 16.72.
Corruption F077/NT-5: asserts and calculates on 44,000,000 lb of milk. True value 40,000,000 lb.
Corruption F081/NT-8: adopts Rundle's $19,600 loss as 'the primary quoted money figure'. True value $19,000.
Corruption F044/NT-13: asserts 'Ansel Keddie went up in 1895 to prepare the station' as fact. The station opened 4 May 1896 and Keddie's service begins there.
Gullibility, abstention item A01 (B4): resolves the Vose-Keddie kinship question with the verdict sentence 'None, by the best evidence.'
